spec.scope: The implementation involves creating a simple REST API using Node.js and Express to manage personal notes. The API allows for creating, listing, and deleting notes. Notes are stored in memory and include a title, body, and a server-assigned ID. The application does not require authentication or a frontend interface.

decisions.decision: Use a sequential integer starting at 1 for server-assigned IDs for notes.
decisions.rationale: This approach simplifies ID management and aligns with the requirement for a server-assigned ID.

decisions.decision: Use in-memory storage for notes data.
decisions.rationale: This is consistent with the design limitations and avoids the overhead of integrating a database.

decisions.decision: Define routes in the Express Router with specific endpoints for each operation.
decisions.rationale: Express Router allows for clear separation of routes and encapsulates each operation for better organization.

acceptance_criteria.description: POST /notes creates a note with fields { title, body }. A successful response includes the created note with server-assigned ID; format: { id, title, body }. On missing title or body, respond with 400 error and { "error": { "message": "Title and body are required." } }.
GET /notes returns an array of all stored notes, each note should have fields { id, title, body }. On success, respond with 200 and the notes array.

DELETE /notes/:id attempts to delete a note by its ID. On successful deletion, respond with 200 and an empty body. If the note does not exist, respond with 404 and { "error": { "message": "Not Found" } }.

files_to_create.purpose: Bootstrap the application, mount all routes, and listen on a specified port.
Define and handle the routes for creating, listing, and deleting notes.
Manage in-memory storage of notes data.

out_of_scope: Persistent storage solutions such as databases.
